title: Probe contract versioning and grace-period negotiation to prevent autoscaler flapping
creator: Jonah Park
description:
Problem: We are seeing periodic autoscaler thrash in multi-region clusters where mismatches between service readiness/liveness semantics and the autoscaler's aggregation window cause rapid scale-down then scale-up cycles, violating p99 latency SLOs. Root causes observed include: probe implementations with different failure-to-ready thresholds across language runtimes, clients sending aggressive probes during deployment ramps, and lack of a formal contract between runtime pods and the autoscaler.

Goal: Define a lightweight 'probe contract' and a runtime-autoscaler negotiation for grace periods and scoring, implement adapters and reconciler changes, and validate with synthetic workloads to stop flapping without increasing steady-state latency or violating resource constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Probe contract spec published in docs/reliability/probe-contract.md describing semantics, required fields, and versioning
Runtime exposes probe version and expected grace window via metadata annotation (or readiness API) in all supported languages
Autoscaler reads probe metadata and applies negotiation logic: min_grace, max_hysteresis, and scoring weights
Integration test harness (synthetic client) simulates regional failover and demonstrates >95% reduction in autoscaler oscillation events compared to baseline under controlled ramp scenarios
No measurable regression in p50/p95 latency for steady-state traffic across canary runs (monitoring dashboards and runbook validated)
Rollout plan with canary toggle and automatic rollback if scale oscillation exceeds threshold
tasks: Draft probe contract spec and versioning rules (owner: Reliability) - TODO: get signoff from runtime leads
Add runtime metadata endpoint/annotation to return probe_version, expected_grace_secs, and failure_score_weights (ENG runtime teams)
Extend autoscaler reconciler to: read probe metadata, compute a negotiated grace window, and apply hysteresis scoring in decision path
Implement synthetic client harness that can run multi-region ramp tests and record oscillation metrics
Create dashboards and alerts for oscillation_count, probe_mismatch_rate, and negotiated_grace_distribution
Write unit and integration tests; run on staging cluster with canary traffic
Prepare rollout plan and QA checklist for runtime-1.20 release
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Adding negotiation may increase time-to-ready for some services and affect latency SLOs. Mitigation: limit negotiated grace to conservative upper bound and run canary to monitor latency metrics.

Risk: Older runtimes that can't expose metadata will be treated with a safe default that may be conservative. Mitigation: provide a migration shim and a migration report to track remaining legacy instances.
Risk: Bug in scoring logic could bias scale-down suppression and cause resource waste. Mitigation: feature flagged toggle + post-deployment resource budget guardrails and alerting.
design_decisions: Use an opt-in probe contract version header initially to minimize blast radius
Negotiate grace in autoscaler as a bounded value between runtime-suggested min and operator-configured max
Score readiness signals over a sliding window with weighted decay rather than binary up/down to reduce sensitivity to short spikes
